title: Public Confessions agree — Wendelin: love also belongs among faith’s acts
source_text: XXXVII. Ex his ergo satis patet, non solum Wittichium fidei corroboratae duntaxat tribuere, quod fidelem certum reddat de impetrata, aut in futurum obtinenda remissione peccatorum; quandoquidem non tantum cum eo consentiunt privati Doctores a nobis citati, sed & ipsae Reformatorum publicae Confessiones. Nec etiam solus ille est, qui amorem Dei Christique syncerum inter essentiales actus fidei recenset. Idem hac in parte sentit cum eo Wendelinus. Quanquam enim fidei partes ad tres revocat, nimirum, notitiam, assensum, atque fiduciam, docet tamen amorem ad actus quoque fidei pertinere. Probat enim non solum intellectum, sed etiam voluntatem esse subjectum fidei, Quia fides quoque est amor, at amor est actus voluntatis: Quod confirmat testimonio Augustini dicentis, Hoc est credere in Christum, diligere Christum. Christ. Theol. lib. 2. cap. 24. in explicatione Theseos octavae.
pass_a_gloss: From these things therefore it is plain enough that not only Wittich attributes to corroborated faith alone that which makes the faithful sure of remission of sins obtained, or to be obtained in the future; seeing that not only the private Doctors cited by us agree with him, but also the public Confessions of the Reformers themselves. Nor is he alone who reckons sincere love of God and of Christ among the essential acts of faith. In this part Wendelin feels the same with him. For although he reduces the parts of faith to three — namely knowledge, assent, and trust — he yet teaches that love also pertains to the acts of faith. For he proves that not only the intellect but also the will is the subject of faith, Because faith also is love, but love is an act of the will: Which he confirms by the testimony of Augustine saying, This is to believe in Christ, to love Christ. Christian Theology book 2, chapter 24, in the explanation of the eighth Thesis.
pass_b_english: Not only Wittich: private doctors and public Reformed Confessions agree.
Full remitted-certainty belongs to corroborated faith.
Wendelin too: sincere love of God/Christ among faith’s acts.
Though parts are notitia/assensus/fiducia, love still belongs — will as well as intellect.
Augustine: to believe in Christ is to love Christ.
